newsitem.title: INDIA: Fire at India's JNPT hits cargo handling.
newsitem.headline: Fire at India's JNPT hits cargo handling.

text.p: Unloading operations at the Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT) in Bombay were disrupted on Monday for several hours following a fire, port officials said.
They said the fire which broke out late on Sunday night continued to rage till the morning hours on Monday before it was put out.
JNPT chairman R. Vasudevan said the fire had erupted while sulphur was being unloaded from a ship, extensively damaging the conveyor belt system used for handling bulk cargo.
About 3,500 tonnes of sulphur stored in a shed had been destroyed, he said.
"The mechanised bulk handling system is out of order. We are trying to get at least one belt in working condition as we are expecting some import of foodgrains," Vasudevan said.
JNPT has three conveyor belts for mechanised handling of bulk cargo, one each for handling sulphur, urea and foodgrains.
"At the moment our efforts are directed at ensuring that at least one belt is in condition to handle operations within three to four weeks," Vasudevan said.
"The fire had alrerady spread by the time it was noticed. It had also damaged electrical installations including power and control systems," he said.
Vasudevan said the port would examine the possibility of using ship-based equipment such as their own derricks to continue the handling of cargo.
"But this is not something which can be done just like that. We have to see what is possible."
